name: The Cibao campos, Dominican Republic
region: Rural campos of the northern Cibao, from the Creighton-ILAC center in Santiago de los Caballeros

families.label: A farm family in a Cibao campo
families.leaveNote: No paid leave: 54.1% of Dominican workers are informal (Q1 2026). Paid maternity (14 weeks) reaches only the formal regime.
families.health: Covered by SENASA's subsidized plan, but specialists and surgery are in Santiago.

loanOptions.label: A prestamista (moneylender)
loanOptions.note: Prestamistas: about 20% a month, interest only (read with care).

loanOptions.label: Bank microcredit
loanOptions.note: Microcredit averaged 35.8% a year (Superintendencia de Bancos, March 2026).

loanOptions.label: Banco Agrícola, if they can reach it
loanOptions.note: Banco Agrícola lends at 8% (June 2025), if the family can reach it and has title.

families.lifeInsNote: Insurance of all kinds came to 1.4% of GDP, half the Latin American average (2022; read with care).

families.label: A Denver family with a salaried parent
families.leaveNote: Colorado FAMLI: up to 12 paid weeks; about 70% of pay at this salary (90% up to half the state average wage, 50% above).
families.health: Insured through work. Colorado's uninsured rate is 5.9% (2025).
families.loanNote: Average credit-card rate, 21.19% a year (Federal Reserve, Q3 2026).
families.lifeInsNote: 71% of U.S. households earning $150,000+ own life insurance (LIMRA 2024).

families.label: A Denver family whose father does day labor for cash
families.leaveNote: FAMLI needs $2,500 in reported Colorado wages; cash day labor often has none.
families.health: Coverage is uncertain; Denver Health is the city's safety net.
families.loanNote: Colorado caps small loans at 36% a year (Prop 111, 2018).
families.lifeInsNote: 31% of U.S. households earning under $50,000 own life insurance (LIMRA 2024).

shocks.label: A hurricane destroys the crop (hail totals the car here)

options.label: Banco Agrícola
options.src: Banco Agrícola, June 2025 (7% for women-led businesses, 0% for young producers)

options.label: A prestamista
options.src: About 20% a month, interest only until the loan is paid (read with care)

options.label: A san (rotating savings)
options.src: No interest, but you wait for your turn, and storms don't wait

gates.label: Has documented income (a formal job or a crop contract)
Can reach a Banco Agrícola office
Has a san turn coming up

options.label: A small loan under Colorado's cap
options.src: Prop 111 (2018): payday loans capped at 36% a year

options.label: Family who can lend
options.src: Depends on who you know. 63% of U.S. adults could cover $400 in cash.
